 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.2,37,989/- awarded by the Tribunal and the attribution of 50% negligence on him, is in appeal.

2. The Tribunal has taken the view that the claimant had contributed to the accident at 50% and this was because the accident occurred on National Highway-4 which had a width of 100 feet and as per the spot mahazar it was clear that there was sufficient space existing by the side of the lorry.
The Tribunal has also observed that the claimant could have avoided the stationed lorry, but had not done so.
It is to be noticed here that the police have in fact laid a chargesheet against the driver of the lorry, who had admittedly parked the lorry on the Highway.
The insurer in order to attribute negligence has not examined the driver of the lorry.
3. In the light of these facts, the finding of the Tribunal that the claimant had contributed to the accident would be unsustainable.

It is to be stated here that when a lorry was parked on the Highway, the presumption have to be drawn that it was responsible for the accident since lorries are not expected to be parked on the Highway.

I am, therefore, of the view that the attribution of 50%
negligence on the claimant was incorrect and it is held that the driver of the lorry was alone responsible for the accident.

4. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered the following injuries :

6.
The Doctor, who was examined, assessed the disability of the claimant at 50% to the limb and 22% to the whole body.
The Doctor, who treated the claimant had assessed the disability at 22% to the whole body.
The said disability will have to be accepted.

7. As far as income is concerned, though the claimant contended that he was working in Sundaram Finance as an Executive and was earning a salary of Rs.18,500/- per month, no evidence is produced to indicate his monthly income.

In this view of the matter, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which for the accident of the year 2014, would be Rs.8,500/-.
8.

The Tribunal has taken the view that the claimant had not produced any evidence to show that he had lost his employment and it has therefore, refused to award compensation towards 'loss of future Muthuraj H N vs T.S.Sudheer on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184629509/
3 earnings'.

9. The claimant had examined the Deputy Manager of his employer and he had stated that the employer had sent a reminder to the claimant to report for duty to which the claimant had replied that he could not report for duties because he had suffered the accident.
The Manager had also stated that the claimant had worked only for five days.
The fact that the claimant has failed to report for duty after the accident indicates that he has suffered loss of earning capacity.
10. Since the Doctor has assessed the permanent disability to the whole body at 22%, it would be appropriate to assess the functional disability at 22%.
As the disability is assessed at 22%, the future prospects of 40% have to be added to the said income.
As a result of which, the monthly income of the claimant would be Rs.11,900/- [Rs.8,500/- + (Rs.8,500/-x40%)].

The claimant would be therefore entitled for the compensation of Rs.5,65,488/- (Rs.11,900/- x 12 x 18 x 22%) towards 'loss of future income'.
11.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.40,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.50,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
In my view, these sums are just and proper and are therefore affirmed.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.3,15,978/- towards medical expenses and Rs.20,000/- towards 'future medical expenses'.
In my view, both these sums are just and proper and are affirmed.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- towards conveyance, nourishment and nutritious food, in my view, this award is also just and proper and is affirmed.
12. The Tribunal has not awarded any sum towards loss of income during laid up period.

Since the claimant was hospitalised for more than 45 days, it would be appropriate to take the laid up period as four months and award Rs.34,000/- (Rs.8,500/- x 4) towards loss of income during laid up period.

13. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation :

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.10,75,466/- as against Rs.2,37,989/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
15. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
16. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
17. Out of the amount of compensation, 60% is ordered to be invested in any Nationalised Bank for a period of five years and the claimant is entitled to withdraw interest accrued periodically.
The remaining amount of compensation is ordered to be released in favour of the claimant after proper identification.
